quiz.q: According to Aristotle, why is proportionate equality preferred over absolute equality in distributive justice?
options: Treating citizens with unequal societal contributions equally creates a feeling of injustice and triggers rebellion.
Absolute equality undermines the absolute monarch's prerogative to distribute state property without legal restraints.
Proportionate equality guarantees that all citizens receive identical shares of public honors regardless of talent.
Rewarding citizens purely on personal need ensures complete fairness in distributing offices and scarce resources.
quiz.why: Aristotle argued that giving equal rewards to unequals is unjust to the meritorious and provokes revolution.

quiz.q: Why does Aristotle identify polity as the best practicable form of government?
options: It allows philosopher kings to exercise unrestricted knowledge beyond the limitations of written laws.
It represents a middle-class golden mean that balances the arrogance of wealth and ignorance of poverty.
It establishes pure direct democracy where the impoverished majority holds absolute power over the rich.
It concentrates governing power within a wealthy hereditary aristocracy to prevent popular factional conflict.
quiz.why: Polity represents the golden mean between oligarchy and democracy, resting on a trusted, moderate middle class.

quiz.q: On what ground does Aristotle establish the superiority of the rule of law over Plato's philosopher king?
options: Philosopher kings lack philosophical training in contemplation and the world of transcendent forms.
Written law can be modified arbitrarily by individual rulers during times of civil crisis.
Law embodies impersonal collective wisdom across ages, whereas even wise rulers may succumb to passion.
Plato's ideal state entirely rejected legal codes in favor of direct democratic majority decisions.
quiz.why: Law represents impersonal reason and the collective wisdom of generations, avoiding the passions of an individual ruler.

quiz.q: In Aristotle's political theory, what constitutes a revolution, and what is its primary general cause?
options: A violent overthrow of the ruling class driven exclusively by external military defeat.
The total economic transformation of property relations driven by inevitable dialectical class conflict.
A planned constitutional amendment enacted solely through the moderate exercise of executive power.
Any change in the constitutional order, sparked primarily by a psychological feeling of inequality.
quiz.why: For Aristotle, revolution is any political change, most commonly caused by perceived inequality or injustice.
